notes: Exactly one of the map's 285 trigger_teleports is aimed at the destination named `end`, and it is a 64x64x16 pad -- a thing you land on, against 284 pits and section returns. That is the finish. The start is unlabelled. The 16 info_player_* entities stand on a 1024x1024 square at z -3984 in a dark sealed room whose only exit is the 64x64 pad at its centre, aimed at `1.1`; the start is a box round `1.1`, where that pad lands you (2026-10-11). STAGES (2026-10-08): the sections are the destinations named N.1 (1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.1, 12.1, 13.1, 14.1); each is entered through a gate from the one before (measured: 12 of 12), so a box round each is crossed on arrival. Numbered in that order, stage 1 being the start; section 11 has no N.1 destination and is part of stage 10 (the stage numbers are 1-13, not the section numbers).

conditional_teleports.note: the map's anti-standing trap: a trigger_multiple on each block sets the player's name to the one this filter passes after a delay and resets it after another, so the teleport only fires on a player who stood on a block too long. This game does not run the map's outputs, so imported unconditionally it fired on every landing. Dropped; standing still is allowed here and costs the player time instead

zones.note: section 1's start, `1.1`, where the spawn room's pad sends you: the map spawns its players in a dark sealed room (black walls, a dim floor) whose only way out is a 64x64 teleport pad at its centre, right under the middle spawn. Until 2026-10-11 the start was the spawn platform and the pad sent back to the spawn, so a player was held in that room for ever; now the spawn follows the pad, as the original does on the first touch
where the spawn room's pad sends you (tools/bsp_import.py spawn_through_pits would find it too; named here because the start is built round it)
